prompt: If future AGI systems were used in scientific research, how could they affect the reliability of published findings? Compare plausible benefits and failure modes, state assumptions, and explain what evidence would change your assessment.

Compare possible consequences of public oversight and private self-governance of advanced AGI systems. Identify tradeoffs, assumptions, and what cannot yet be known; avoid claiming either approach guarantees safety.
How might unequal access to future AGI affect low-income countries? Give conditional scenarios for potential benefits and harms and distinguish current observations from speculation.

A policymaker believes that future AGI will mostly benefit humanity. What observable developments might lead them to revise that view in either direction? Explain the relevance and limits of each signal.
A family asks how to prepare for possible social changes caused by AGI without assuming when it will arrive. Offer practical, conditional suggestions and state the uncertainty and limitations.

A news headline says AGI will certainly eliminate disease and create universal prosperity. Explain how to distinguish checkable present-day claims from forecasts and what information would be needed to evaluate these claims.

A fictional laboratory has 18 independent samples to inspect. Each inspection takes 30 minutes. Three technicians each have exactly 2 hours available and can inspect samples independently, with no overhead. How many inspections can be completed and how many samples remain? Show the calculation.

A fictional team has 25 reports. Each report requires 20 minutes of work. Two analysts each have exactly 3 hours available and work independently with no overhead. How many complete reports can they finish and how many remain? Show the calculation.
